details: Owner, 27 Oct, answering whether a run that did not finish in its 10 minutes is a failed run under the 2-of-3 majority rule: "7. a" (a = count it as a failed run; the summary names it; two timeouts are red). Today such a run is "not judged" and makes the whole wave red even when the other two passed. Measured 27 Oct: 22 such runs in 21 stored records, none of which would change its record's verdict. Needed before the next paid run, which plays 3 evals at once (owner, 27 Oct: "5. a"), where load may cause more timeouts. Split out of a-wave-run-is-red-when-one-of-a-case-s-3-runs-fa (review finding F5 of that change) so the majority rule lands first: relay sync waits on it.
failing_case: A case with runs PASS, PASS, timed out after 600s: the wave verdict is RED ('1 not judged').
pass_cases: PASS, PASS, timed out: green, and the summary says '2 of 3 runs passed, 1 timed out'.
PASS, timed out, timed out: red.
A falling pass rate counts a timeout as a failed run.
A test fails with the rule disabled.
reason: tests/test_eval_majority.py:73 passes; fails without the fix at da674b4^.
findings.summary: A timed-out eval run counts as one failed run

details: CONFIRMED as fragile, not wrong: the only evidence of the wording is the 3 stored timeouts. The failure direction is
safe (red, not green). Rules/python: data relay does not control goes through one checking parser at the boundary;
the prefix test is that parser, so keeping it in one function is right. A case-insensitive match, or a test pinning the
exact stored text, makes a wording drift visible. Size: 5.
evidence: census of ~/.relay/evals/relay/*.json run errors: 19 'exit 1: Reached maximum number of turns (3)', 3 'timed out after 600s'
failing_case: A run {"error": "Timed out after 600s", "durationSeconds": 600, "graders": [...]} (or "timeout after 600s") in an arm
PASS, PASS, <that run>: timed_out() is False, the run is "not judged", the wave is RED. The owner's rule says it is a
failed run and the case passes 2 of 3. Today's tool writes "timed out after 600s" (3 of 3 stored timeouts), so it is
correct today; the match is on text relay does not control.
fix_hint: Leave as is, or match case-insensitively (re.match(r"timed? ?out", ..., re.I)); either way keep it in timed_out().
pass_cases: {"error": "timed out after 600s"} in PASS, PASS, timeout -> green, "2 of 3 runs passed, 1 timed out".
{"error": "exit 1: Reached maximum number of turns (3)"} in PASS, PASS, error -> red, "1 not judged".
PASS, timeout, timeout -> red, "2 run(s) timed out".
reason: tests/test_eval_timeouts.py capitalised-message test passes (bin/eval-record:60 lowercases); fails at b62f5b2^.
findings.summary: a timeout is recognised only by the prefix of the eval tool's free-text error, so a reworded message silently goes back to 'not judged'

details: CONFIRMED by reading. Docs only; cheap. Size: 5.
evidence: bin/eval-record:7-8 "exit 2 ... when a case fails its majority ... any run was not judged ..."
failing_case: A reader of bin/eval-record's docstring (lines 7-8) or lib/relay_ci.py's (line 13) learns that "any run was not
judged" makes the gate red and nothing about timeouts; they expect PASS, PASS, timed out to be red, while the code
now makes it green.
fix_hint: Add one clause to the docstring at line 8: "a run the eval tool stopped at its time limit is a failed run of the majority, not an unjudged one".
pass_cases: The docstring of bin/eval-record says a run that timed out counts as a failed run of the majority (owner, 27 Oct, "7. a").
The docstring still says any other errored run is not judged and makes the gate red.
reason: tests/test_eval_timeouts.py docstring test passes; bin/eval-record docstring states the rule; fails at b62f5b2^.
findings.summary: the module docstring still lists the red conditions without the timeout rule
